title: Keyboard and Mouse Control
description: Buttons type letters on your computer, and letters you send move the mouse.

source.title: Arduino docs: Keyboard and Mouse Control

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Leonardo and its USB cable, a breadboard, 5 × pushbutton, 5 × 10 kΩ resistor, and some jumper wires.
Push the U button in across the middle gap: two legs above the gap, two below.
hints: The two legs in one column (above and below the gap) are always joined inside the button.
Pressing joins the left column to the right column.
steps.goal: Put the U button across the middle gap.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the U button's left column (top half) to pin 2 on the Arduino.
hints: Any hole in that column works.
Pin 2 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.
steps.goal: Connect one side of the U button to pin 2.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's 5V pin → the red + row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. The U button's right column (bottom half) → that same row.
hints: When you press, 5V flows through the button to the pin.
steps.goal: Connect the other side of the U button to 5V.

steps.clip: Push a 10 kΩ resistor in: one leg in the U button's left column (bottom half), the other leg in an empty column.
hints: This is a pull-down: it keeps the pin LOW until you press.
Without it the pin 'floats' and reads random values.
steps.goal: Put a 10 kΩ resistor on the U button's pin side.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. The 10 kΩ resistor's other leg → that same row.
hints: Now the pin reads LOW, and HIGH only while you press.
steps.goal: Connect the pull-down resistor to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. Open a text editor and press the buttons: the letters appear. Send u, d, l, r or m from the Serial Monitor to move or click the mouse.
